title: ARC Control Agent
description: An agent is the principal ARC Control authorizes. It is never a human: a human acts through the console or an approval, an agent acts through the gateway. Every agent has an owner who is accountable for what it does.

id.description: Opaque identifier assigned by ARC Control.

name.description: Stable handle used in policies and audit records, e.g. "finance-agent".

status.description: Only `active` may act. The gateway checks for that positively rather than excluding the states it knows about, so a state added here can never accidentally be granted the right to act. `draft` is registered but not cleared; `retired` is withdrawn permanently and has its credentials revoked.

environment.description: Deployment environment; policies may scope to it.

owner.description: The human or team accountable for this agent. Resolves the `owner` approver selector.

roles.description: Roles the agent holds. Policies match on these rather than naming agents directly.

declaredTools.description: Tools the agent declares it needs. Advisory: policy still decides every call.

governance.description: Business and governance context. Optional on purpose: an agent registered through the 1.x API has none, and the honest representation of that is an absent record that coverage analysis reports as a gap — not a synthesised default that makes an ungoverned agent look governed.

purpose.description: What this agent exists to do, in business language.

criticality.description: The organization’s judgement, not something inferred from the tools the agent holds: the business consequence of a wrong action is not a property of the API it calls.

promptReview.description: The latest static review of the agent's system prompt (2.3). The prompt itself is never stored: only its grade, failed check ids and a digest.

retiredAt.description: Set when the agent was retired, so a retirement is dated rather than implied.
